name: Praecipua
description: A star 29 parsecs away, 7.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: radius 7.909 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 28.492 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.053) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: effective temperature 4745 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.063)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.73 from 2013ApJ...764...78R; the 12 published values span log g 2.5 to 3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: distance 29.087 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 29 parsecs away, 7.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 28 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,745 K, so 7.909 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 53229: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 46 Leonis Minoris
quotes.card: 46 Leonis Minoris, also named Praecipua, is the brightest star in the constellation of Leo Minor.
quotes.introduction: It is of spectral class K0+III-IV and of magnitude 3.83.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 738259665062428416 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
